questions.prompt: What is the difference between the Well-Architected Framework (WAF) and the Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF)?

options.text: WAF guides an individual workload's design; CAF guides the organization's whole cloud journey
They are two names for the same checklist
WAF is about billing; CAF is about networking

questions.explanation: WAF guides the design of a single workload (via the five pillars); CAF guides the organization's overall cloud journey — strategy, readiness (landing zones), governance, and management.

questions.prompt: Which of these are pillars of the Azure Well-Architected Framework? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The five pillars are Reliability, Security, Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence, and Performance Efficiency. 'Marketing Reach' is not one of them.

questions.prompt: The framework that guides an organization's entire cloud journey (strategy, readiness, governance, management) is the Cloud ____ Framework.
questions.explanation: The Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) guides the whole organizational journey; the Well-Architected Framework guides each individual workload.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of a good architecture process.

items.text: Evaluate the design against the five pillars

questions.explanation: Understand requirements, evaluate against the pillars, make and document deliberate trade-offs, and revisit as needs change.

questions.prompt: Match each Well-Architected pillar to its focus.

pairs.right: Staying available and recovering from failure
Getting the most value per dollar
Using resources effectively and scaling to demand

questions.explanation: Reliability = availability/recovery; Security = protection; Cost Optimization = value per dollar; Performance Efficiency = effective, scalable resource use.
